title: Maple Street Retail - outreach playnotes
body:
Quick scratchpad for Maple Street Retail (MSR) outreach — mix of research, cold-email drafts, and objection handling. Do not over-engineer — this is just my working surface.

Account snapshot:
- Company: Maple Street Retail (mid-market omni-channel retail chain)
- HQ: Chicago, IL
- Estimated stores: ~420 US stores + ecommerce site
- Estimated engineering org: ~35 eng, 6-8 ML/AI folks (job postings hint)
- Current stack signals: uses GCP (billing tags), references to Redis/Firestore in job posts, evidence of serving infra migration in Oct 2023 blog post

Key contacts (public + outreach status):
- Lina Peters — Head of ML Platforms (LinkedIn: lina-peters-msr) — primary target for platform fit. Cold email 10/25, follow-up 11/05 (left VM).
- Aaron Cho — Director of Product (omnichannel) — warm intro via Mara (partner). Intro scheduled 11/08.
- Vinod Iyer — CIO (enterprise procurement) — likely fiscal decision, long cycle.

Why Redwood could be interesting to them (explicit signals):
- They mention "reduce per-order fraud detection latency" in job posting (real-time inference use case). Redwood Optimize + Dedicated could materially cut per-token/unit costs for embedded models and reduce tail latency.
- Multi-environment control: they run part of stack in VPC and have compliance needs for payments. Private deployments offering (VPC + KMS) is a clear checklist win.
- Observability request: postings request "model-level observability" during deployments — Redwood Console features align well.

Immediate hypothesis for pilot / initial use case:
- Pilot replacing or augmenting a policy scoring microservice: ingest order context -> run LLM-based risk/heuristic enrichments -> return signaling to fraud scoring.
- Success metrics: 95th pct latency < 250ms (for scoring path), cost per 1k requests <= $X (TBD after conversation), measurable lift in detection precision or reduction in manual review volume.

Risk & unknowns / due diligence items (questions for discovery call):
- Are they currently using any LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, internal)? If yes, which latencies / cost breakpoints are they currently seeing?
- Can their fraud scoring path tolerate a small additional hop (we need to confirm end-to-end SLA)?
- Data residency/PCI implications for order payloads — would they be comfortable with tokenization/PII redaction or require on-prem?
- Existing infra constraints: GPU hosting policy; procurement timeline for Reserved Capacity; any existing supplier lock-ins.

Cold email drafts (pick lean version for initial outreach):
- Short variant (for Lina):
  Subject: A quick note on reducing inference latency for MSR fraud signals
  Hey Lina — noticed MSR hiring for real-time ML infra and thought it might be relevant: we helped a mid-market retailer cut model inference tail latency by ~40% while decreasing per-request cost using a mix of prefix caching + quantized model variants. Would you be open to 20 minutes to see if the same levers map to your fraud path?
  -Jordan

- Longer variant (technical, send after intro):
  Subject: Example pilot: <10ms cache-hit enrichment for order scoring at MSR scale
  Lina — quick follow on from my note: sketch of a pilot we typically run (2–4 week):
  1) ingest anonymized sample of order payloads (no PII),
  2) run 1–2 candidate models via Redwood Private/Dedicated, measure 95/99th latency and cost per 1k evals,
  3) enable prefix/KV caching for common order patterns and run A/B vs current ML enrichments,
  4) dashboard + alerting wired into your SRE/alerts.
  Outcome: concrete latency/cost numbers and a short rollout plan. If that sounds useful, can we get 20–30m next week?

Handling objections (scripted counters / notes to self):
- "We already use x provider (OpenAI/Anthropic)":
  Counter: "Totally — many teams use multiple endpoints. We position Redwood as a serving layer that can orchestrate model variants (hosted/open) and optimize cost/latency via batching, caching, and quantization — not a forced migration. A light pilot can show econ delta quickly."

- "Procurement will block on Dedicated/Private pricing":
  Counter: "Offer a 30-day proof (hosted) to show value; if compliance is gating, focus discovery on minimal data isolation (VPC peering + tokenization) and pull in our security lead early. Note: highlight Enterprise pricing playbook with finance team — Diego has a stub playbook + term sheet we can reuse (ask Diego for copy)."

- "We can't expose order PII outside our VPC":
  Counter: "We can do a data-in-place pilot using Private deployment in their cloud account (bring-your-own keys). Also propose a synthetic-data run to validate model behavior before any real data touch."

Meeting prep checklist (for discovery):
- Ask for a sample SLO for the fraud scoring path (p95/p99 latency budget).
- Clarify volume patterns (peak orders per minute, seasonal peaks).
- Which fields in order payload are considered sensitive / PCI? Any redaction requirements?
- Who’s decision-maker for a pilot vs procurement? Typical procurement timeline?
- Get a read on current tracing/observability stack (Grafana/Tempo/Datadog).

Internal asks / tasks (assign):
- Maya: can you pull any public MSR tech blog mentions we might have missed? Slack DMed. (due 11/06)
- Diego: send standard 30-day hosted pilot terms + example pricing bands used with similar retailers. (due 11/04)
- Jordan (me): prep a 15m demo script showing cache-hit vs cold path on sample payloads. Need small synthetic dataset. (due 11/07)

Notes-to-self / rough hypothesis numbers (ballpark; verify with Diego):
- If we achieve 30–50% cache hit on common order prefixes, effective p95 token work could drop ~40% -> big cost delta.
- Ops ask: ensure fallback paths to smaller quantized model variant to keep p99 under budget during spikes.

Open questions / follow-ups after next call:
- Confirm Lina's availability and if Aaron can invite an SRE on call.
- Get anonymized sample of order events (one-week window) or synthetic generator pattern.
- Sales ops: what discount bands apply for 12-month Dedicated commit for mid-market retail?

Slack shorthand (internal updates):
- TL;DR: targeting MSR for fraud-enrichment pilot. Primary ask: prove latency and cost improvement via caching + quantization. Need sample payloads + Lina intro.

Random thoughts / brainstorm (unstructured):
- Could propose a "store-level offline cache" idea: precompute embeddings/features for common SKUs to reduce token work on PO lines.
- Consider pairing Redwood Optimize runbook with their A/B test cadence to measure manual review reduction (business metric buyers will care).

End of scratchpad. Keep short notes here as they happen.

-- Jordan
